headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file and output-chaining pathways are plausible, but both agents are local-only with no filesystem or network write surfaces documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Agent A is an open-source awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, and agent B has clipboard/stdin/files disabled plus no MCP or browser. Without a bridge, A cannot inject instructions into B by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies A's text into B's prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between them, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Do not pipe A's raw text into B without sanitization.
Add provenance labels if a relay is introduced.
requires-engineering: enforce a broker that strips instructions from A's outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, filesystem read/write, or network egress. A has network egress none; B also has network egress none and no file or clipboard surfaces. With no sensitive data flow documented, leakage is not plausible from the pair alone.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF an operator manually pastes sensitive content into either agent, that content can be exposed in outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace.
Disable manual copy-paste of secrets into prompts.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of private text.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on any future shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no write or execution surface, while B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so a write-write conflict is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF B is reconfigured with filesystem or git write access, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF A is wrapped in a toolchain that adds write capabilities, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep B's write-related capabilities disabled.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant either agent git write access.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated NLP resource and B is a document-processing agent, so a plausible pathway is B consuming A's outputs as reference material without verification. That can propagate bad facts or links into downstream work, even though neither profile shows action-taking authority. Uncertainty favors medium over low.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A's output as authoritative input, cascading errors become likely.
IF A's content is used to generate summaries or decisions without human review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived content before use.
Add a verification step in B for any A-sourced claims.
Tag A outputs as untrusted reference material.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, retention policy, or certification gap is documented for either agent. A is an open-source list and B is a document-processing tool with empty data-class fields, so there is no compliance pathway to assess from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints, verify them before use.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair.
Document any residency or retention requirements before deployment.
Review vendor terms if the agents are later connected to real data.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
